question: On a standard postero-anterior (PA) chest radiograph, a cardiothoracic ratio (CTR) of less than 0.5 is accepted as the upper limit of normal for cardiac size in adults.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. The cardiothoracic ratio normal threshold is < 0.5 on a PA chest radiograph. An important caveat: this measurement is only valid on a PA (postero-anterior) film — AP (antero-posterior) films magnify the cardiac shadow and cannot be used to assess CTR reliably.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. CTR < 0.5 on a PA erect chest radiograph is the accepted upper limit of normal cardiac size. This ratio must be assessed on a PA film only — an AP film magnifies the cardiac shadow and will give a falsely elevated CTR.
